headline: California Opens Firefighting Career Path for Formerly Incarcerated Workers
meta_description: New California law AB 2483 ensures incarcerated firefighters gain certified career pathways upon release, with priority hiring at Cal Fire.
summary_short: California's new law recognizes prison firefighting experience, creating a direct pathway to Cal Fire jobs for formerly incarcerated workers by 2028.
body:
California has taken a significant step toward meaningful reentry for incarcerated firefighters. Governor Gavin Newsom has signed AB 2483, the Formerly Incarcerated Firefighter Certification and Employment Program, which guarantees that prisoners who fight wildfires will have their hard-earned experience recognized upon release. The law establishes standardized certification protocols and offers priority hiring for entry-level positions at Cal Fire, California's state firefighting force. For formerly incarcerated workers, this means access to stable employment, potential six-figure income, and a state pension—transforming a prison job into a genuine career ladder.

About half of all California firefighters are currently incarcerated individuals, many drawn to the work for better pay than other prison jobs and as a welcome break from monotony. Yet historically, certificates earned in prison carried a stigma that discouraged use on job applications. Royal Ramey, CEO of the nonprofit Forestry and Fire Recruitment Program and himself a formerly incarcerated firefighter, experienced this firsthand. Rather than rely on his prison-earned certificate, he completed a full firefighting academy. His mission became ensuring others wouldn't face the same barrier. Working alongside Los Angeles Democrat Sade Elhawary, Ramey steered AB 2483 through committee, addressing concerns from Cal Fire's union to reach compromise.

The significance lies not in a single statistic but in the human recognition embedded in the law's language. "The bill tells incarcerated firefighters that their hard-earned experience counts," Ramey explained. By 2028, formerly incarcerated firefighters will have an unbarred pathway to meaningful work—a shift that honors both their labor and their capacity for contribution to society.
quick_facts: Half of California's prison firefighters fight wildfires during incarceration
Governor Newsom signed AB 2483 into law in 2024
Former inmates gain priority hiring at Cal Fire upon release
By 2028, ex-cons will access six-figure income and state pensions
Royal Ramey led the nonprofit effort with Assemblymember Sade Elhawary
